title: Shared two-machine rules: one web-canonical file both repos follow (modes, claiming, unattended nights)
acceptance: New ritmofit_dev_plan/two-machine-rules.md is the one shared rules file for both repos. It covers machines and their limits, one-machine and both-machines modes, claiming, owner decisions as GitHub records, who finishes a PR, messaging, task status at approval (iOS RF-1038), and unattended merge nights (pre-approval issue, queue eligibility, merge bar, hard stops, CI hygiene, claims and hygiene).

AGENTS.md "Two-machine conductors" points to that file instead of holding the rules; the stale text saying the Air runs the iOS CI runner and keeps the RitmoFit-CI simulator is gone (iOS CI runs on the Neo since iOS #86).

AGENTS.md "Never granted" allows an agent to apply owner-approved only to a PR covered by a night's pre-approval issue, after that night's merge bar passes, with a comment citing the issue and head SHA. Each repo keeps its own merge mechanics.

evidence.summary: Owner decisions (2026-11-04, Neo session), verbatim: the silo ends; one machine works both repos within limits; both on, claim per task; web-canonical file with an iOS parity check; shared scope is machine rules plus unattended nights; owner-approved via a night's pre-approval issue; the Neo writes it now ("Go as written").

Fresh-context /code-review high found 10 issues (eligibility list looser than owner-gate, AGENTS.md permission and push-voids text, wrong snapshot list, night claim vs draft-first, label/merge order, stale record and references, present-tense iOS parity, handoff PR, issue template rendering); all fixed on the branch.

resolution: ritmofit_dev_plan/two-machine-rules.md is the shared, owner-gated rules file; AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, start-session and the deployment runbook point to it, and the merge policy names the unattended-night exception. The iOS copy and its parity check are iOS RF-1041.
